Decision Table for the 3+3 Design

Source: R/decision_table_3p3.R
decision_table_3p3.Rd

Tabulate the dose assignment rule of the traditional 3+3 design used by oc_3p3 and sim_3p3: for every number of DLTs among the three or six patients treated at the current dose, the decision taken during dose escalation and, for mtd_rule = "expand", during the search for the MTD that follows it.

Usage

decision_table_3p3(mtd_rule = c("previous", "expand"))

Arguments

mtd_rule

Character scalar, either "previous" or "expand". The definition of the MTD, as in oc_3p3. Defaults to "previous".

Value

An object of class decision_table_3p3, which is a data frame with one row per state of the current dose and the columns

stage

"escalation" for dose escalation, or "search" for the search for the MTD, which only mtd_rule = "expand" has.

n

Number of patients treated at the current dose, 3 or 6.

n_tox

Number of patients with a DLT, from 0 to n.

decision

Decision code. During escalation, "E" escalates to the next higher dose, "S" treats three more patients at the current dose and "STOP" stops escalation, this dose and all higher doses being too toxic. During the search, "S" treats three more patients at the current dose, "MTD" selects it as the MTD and "D" moves the search to the next lower dose.

The definition of the MTD is stored in the attribute mtd_rule. The object has print and plot methods.

Details

During escalation three patients are treated at the current dose. No DLT escalates, one DLT adds three more patients at the same dose, and two or more stop escalation. With six patients, at most one DLT escalates and two or more stop escalation. Escalating from the highest dose also ends escalation.

With mtd_rule = "previous" the MTD is the dose below the one at which escalation stopped, or the highest dose when it was escalated from, and no MTD is selected when escalation stops at the starting dose. With mtd_rule = "expand" the search starts at the dose below the one at which escalation stopped, or at the highest dose when it was escalated from. A dose with three patients receives three more; a dose with at most one DLT out of six is selected as the MTD, and one with two or more passes the search to the next lower dose. No MTD is selected when the search moves below the starting dose.

Every number of DLTs from 0 to n is listed for six patients, although in a trial the six patients at a dose during escalation always include one DLT among the first three. The search examines only doses that were escalated from, so a dose with three patients has no DLT there, and only that state is listed.

The rules are those of oc_3p3: the tests follow this table through every possible course of a trial and obtain the operating characteristics of oc_3p3().

See also

print.decision_table_3p3, plot.decision_table_3p3, oc_3p3, boin_decision_table

Examples

decision_table_3p3()
#> 3+3 decision table, MTD rule: previous (the dose below the one declared too toxic)
#> 
#> Dose escalation
#>  Patients DLTs Decision                          
#>  3        0    Escalate                          
#>  3        1    Treat 3 more patients at this dose
#>  3        >= 2 Stop escalation                   
#>  6        <= 1 Escalate                          
#>  6        >= 2 Stop escalation                   
#> 
#> Stop escalation means that this dose and all higher doses are too
#> toxic. The MTD is the dose below the one at which escalation stopped,
#> and no MTD is selected when escalation stops at the starting dose. When
#> the highest dose is escalated from, it is the MTD.

# The other definition of the MTD adds the search for the MTD
decision_table_3p3(mtd_rule = "expand")
#> 3+3 decision table, MTD rule: expand (the highest dose with at most 1 DLT in 6)
#> 
#> Dose escalation
#>  Patients DLTs Decision                          
#>  3        0    Escalate                          
#>  3        1    Treat 3 more patients at this dose
#>  3        >= 2 Stop escalation                   
#>  6        <= 1 Escalate                          
#>  6        >= 2 Stop escalation                   
#> 
#> Search for the MTD
#>  Patients DLTs Decision                          
#>  3        0    Treat 3 more patients at this dose
#>  6        <= 1 Select this dose as the MTD       
#>  6        >= 2 Move to the next lower dose       
#> 
#> Stop escalation means that this dose and all higher doses are too
#> toxic. The search for the MTD starts at the dose below the one at which
#> escalation stopped, or at the highest dose when it is escalated from.
#> No MTD is selected when the search moves below the starting dose.
